CURRENT BEHAVIOR REPORT (operator-observed, 2026-08-13, post-1739-merge):

A third occurrence of the restartable-lock pathology, AFTER 1739 merged. An orphaned compactor (PPID 1) spawned from a temporary `wt-close` worktree ran 12+ minutes and held the shared store lock for 5+ minutes, blocking a queued transactional ticket write. The operator gracefully terminated only its isolated process group so the queued write could finish — the same manual-kill remedy this ticket exists to make unnecessary.

Mechanism (why old code ran after the fix merged): the `wt-close` worktree's close operations ran via the MAIN checkout's venv (`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.venv`, an editable install of the main checkout's working tree), and the main checkout had not been advanced to the merged 1739. The operation-linked trigger therefore detached a sweep executing the PRE-1739 per-ticket history-walk code. Any environment whose rebar build predates 50cc45f0d1 will keep reproducing this until its checkout/install advances — the fix's deployment lags its merge wherever editable installs track stale checkouts.

Implications for this ticket's plan: (1) reinforces the core case — all three incidents were resolved by a human manually identifying and killing a holder the tooling described only as a bare pid; the `op=compact-sweep` stamp and stated-remedy error text would have made each self-service; (2) consider the stamp carrying the code version/commit of the holder, so an operator can see at a glance that a holder is running superseded code.
